nodes.label: Why the min-h-full Wrapper Attempt Failed
nodes.norm_label: why the min-h-full wrapper attempt failed
nodes.rationale: A min-h-full wrapper around children placed the absolutely positioned grid above any page whose root was not positioned, because absolute siblings paint over unpositioned in-flow content regardless of DOM order; this also broke PageFrame's own min-h-full so the overview's column borders stopped at content bottom. Fixed by making the grid sticky top-0 z-[-1] h-0 inside an isolate, [container-type:size] main sized h-[100cqh]: sticky with zero height takes no space, cqh sizes to the scroll area rather than the viewport, and z-[-1] inside isolate paints below in-flow content.

nodes.label: D1: Database approach (PGlite)
nodes.rationale: PGlite chosen, spike first, because it preserves the existing query surface and migrations rather than requiring a rewrite.

nodes.label: PGlite connection mutex
nodes.rationale: PGlite has a single connection; a mutex serialises connect() and queues plain queries behind an open transaction. Proved by spike: with the mutex removed, a stray bare query read an uncommitted row before commit, so the mutex is required for transactional correctness.

nodes.label: Phase 3: PGlite driver registry (no external database)
nodes.norm_label: phase 3: pglite driver registry (no external database)
nodes.rationale: Recommended over SQLite repositories because PGlite (WASM Postgres in-process) keeps all ~100 query sites, the 12 migrations and the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED job queue unchanged, whereas SQLite would need ~100 query sites and ~20 tests rewritten off Postgres-isms for no gain the user can see. The seam is db/pool.ts as a driver registry (HELIX_DB=pglite|pg) with a mutex serializing PGlite's single connection.

nodes.label: Code review of commit 50fb19c
nodes.rationale: Found and fixed before release: the bootstrap key could be revoked and lock the desktop app out (fixed with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET revoked_at = NULL and UI refusal to revoke it); closePool() ordering could force-kill PGlite mid-write; the sweeper's first run ignored resultTtlHours and running jobs; PGlite errors logged bound parameters; /app/ 404'd; mode.ts used ?? for the MCP URL; openapi.yaml still described the multi-tenant model.

nodes.label: E: is exFAT (no symlinks constraint)
nodes.rationale: exFAT has no symlinks, forcing pnpm node-linker=hoisted; readlink returns EISDIR on a regular file, fatal to webpack, so next build must happen on C: via robocopy, and Turbopack must never be retried on this exFAT monorepo.

nodes.label: D16: Graceful stop via IPC
nodes.rationale: Windows has no SIGTERM, so the supervisor spawns the API with an IPC channel and sends a shutdown message; the API runs the same close sequence as SIGTERM, and the supervisor force-kills the tree after 10s (raised from 3s after code review found PGlite could be force-killed mid-write).

nodes.label: D5: Scope of the session (Phases 3-7)

nodes.label: Confirm Gate Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every tool that changes Canvas takes a confirm bool defaulting false; called without it, the tool returns a preview and makes no mutating request. Nothing changes in Canvas by accident.

nodes.label: PageList Page-Cap Disclosure
nodes.rationale: get_all() now returns a PageList carrying whether the 1000-item page cap was hit, so a listing tool states the shown count rather than silently dropping items past the cap with no indication to the model or user.

nodes.label: Enrich Verification-Against-Fetched-Text Rule
nodes.rationale: Every returned value is verified against text the API fetched: the model must quote the grounding passage, which is checked against the source page, and the value checked against the passage. Anything that fails becomes null with a reason rather than a low-confidence guess.

nodes.label: Extract Field-Grounding Rule
nodes.rationale: A field with no grounding span in its source is dropped and reported in `dropped`, rather than returned, because a plausible number nobody can check is the expensive failure. A URL that could not be read is a warning, not a failed request.

nodes.label: Shared-Secret Auth Design Intent
nodes.rationale: Claude on the web reaches an MCP server from Anthropic's servers, not the browser, so localhost will not do; the server needs a public HTTPS URL, meaning anything that can reach the URL can use the Canvas token, so the server refuses to listen beyond localhost until a shared secret is set. The connector dialog takes a URL and nothing else, which is why the secret goes in the path as /s/<token>.

nodes.label: Claims guard (WEBSITE.md §11)
nodes.rationale: Applies to every user-facing string; the site copy never states counts, to avoid unverifiable marketing claims.

nodes.label: Fingerprint perturbation seed (keyed HMAC)
nodes.rationale: Seeding from a public id would let a tracker invert the mask and read the true hardware hash, so the seed must never be derivable from public data — keyed HMAC only.

nodes.label: Grounding check (enrich)
nodes.rationale: A citation that fails verification is the control working, so the grounding check must never be softened to raise enrich yield.

nodes.label: D10: Publish to helix-releases

nodes.label: D11: Autoupdate wired in 2.0.0

nodes.label: Document API Dispatch Design
nodes.rationale: The /document endpoint dispatches rather than reimplements: each operation keeps its own multipart parsing, upload ceiling, in-flight cap and result cache, so a request behaves identically whether it arrives at /document or the original path.
